score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial B2B database market: at least 6 major vendors (BookYourData with 25,419 verified personal trainers at 97% accuracy rate, InfoGlobalData with CASS certified personal trainers list at 90% accuracy, Exact Data with 10+ years as fitness trainer list industry leader, ContactOut with highly accurate meticulously verified fitness trainer database, Influencers.club with monthly-refreshed personal trainers database, Scrap.io with 67K+ fitness professionals) currently selling personal trainer and certified fitness professional email databases with documented pricing at $0.10-$2.00 per contact (InfoGlobalData quote), indicating sustained high-value B2B demand. Four distinct high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) Gym management and fitness studio software vendors (Mindbody serving 70,000+ fitness and wellness businesses globally at $119-$399/month for scheduling, client management, marketing automation, and payment processing generating $1,428-$4,788/year LTV, Zen Planner at $127-$397/month for gym management software, Glofox for boutique fitness studios at $110-$279/month, Pike13 for class-based fitness businesses, TrueCoach for online personal training at $29-$199/month, Wodify for CrossFit boxes at $99-$299/month, GymMaster for gym chains, ClubReady for health clubs, Virtuagym, TeamUp) selling all-in-one platforms for class scheduling, member check-ins, billing automation, client communication, marketing funnels, and mobile apps — software vendors pay $3,000-$8,000/year for certified personal trainer databases to acquire gym owners, studio owners, and independent trainers as customers; (2) Fitness equipment manufacturers and distributors (Rogue Fitness for strength equipment and CrossFit gear, TRX suspension trainers, Peloton for connected fitness bikes and treadmills, NordicTrack, Bowflex home gym systems, Precor commercial gym equipment, Life Fitness cardholders and ellipticals, Hammer Strength, Matrix Fitness, Technogym, Nautilus, FreeMotion, Assault Fitness air bikes and runners, Concept2 rowers, Keiser bikes, Woodway treadmills, Battle Ropes, kettlebells, dumbbells, resistance bands, foam rollers) selling to personal trainers purchasing equipment for home studios, boot camps, and small training facilities with typical equipment packages ranging $5,000-$50,000 for fully equipped training space; (3) Fitness education and continuing education providers (NASM offering 50+ continuing education courses and specializations at $99-$699 per course with CPT recertification requiring 2.0 CEUs or 20 hours every 2 years, ACE requiring 2.0 CEUs over 2-year cycle, ISSA offering 30+ specialization certifications, Precision Nutrition coaching certification at $999-$1,299, AFAA group fitness specializations, NSCA CSCS exam prep, functional training certifications, corrective exercise specialist programs, nutrition coaching credentials, senior fitness specialist, youth fitness specialist, pre/postnatal specialist, sports performance coach — typical annual CE spend per certified trainer ranges $200-$800 to maintain certification and add specializations); and (4) Fitness business services including liability insurance providers (K&K Insurance for personal trainer professional liability at $150-$400/year, Philadelphia Insurance Companies, RPS Bollinger fitness insurance, ACE-Fitpro insurance program), payment processing for personal training sessions, client management and CRM tools, nutrition software (My Fitness Pal Premium for trainers, Cronometer, RP Diet App), online coaching platforms (Trainerize at $5-$60/month per trainer for 10-300 clients, TrueCoach, My PT Hub, PT Distinction), client assessment software (FMS screens, InBody body composition scanners at $2,500-$4,500, Tanita scales), marketing agencies specializing in personal trainer lead generation, website builders for fitness professionals, merchant services for gym payments, and tax preparation for self-employed trainers. Excellent public registry access via USREPS (United States Registry of Exercise Professionals) maintained by CREP (Commission on Reforming Exercise Professionals) listing 130,000+ currently certified professionals from member organizations — anyone earning an NCCA accredited or ISO 17024-compliant certification from member organizations (ACE, NASM, ACSM, NSCA, AFAA, ISSA, and 20+ others) is automatically registered in USREPS directory free of charge; registry is fully public and searchable at usreps.org/registry/ with no authentication required. Additional public directories: NASM maintains public credential verification directory at directory.nasm.org for employers and gyms to verify certified personal trainers; ACSM provides profinder directory at acsm.org/certification/professional-resources/profinder/ to find ACSM certified professionals. Massive total addressable market: 130,000+ currently certified exercise professionals in USREPS registry alone (ACE, NASM, ACSM, NSCA, AFAA, ISSA combined), with broader fitness industry employment estimated at 384,000+ fitness trainers and instructors per BLS May 2023 data (includes non-certified instructors and group fitness), and commercial vendor databases claiming 25,000-67,000 verified personal trainer contacts confirming substantial professional population. Zero PII restrictions — professional certifications and credentials are voluntary public records maintained by certification organizations to enable employer verification, with USREPS explicitly designed as public registry for healthcare providers and employers to find and verify certified exercise professionals. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape USREPS registry (searchable web interface, likely requires iterative queries or web scraping), augment with NASM directory and ACSM profinder, normalize credential types across certifying organizations (CPT, CSCS, CES, PES, GFI, health coach, clinical exercise physiologist mapping to standard nomenclature), deduplicate multi-credentialed professionals (many trainers hold multiple certifications like NASM-CPT plus CES corrective exercise specialist), geocode addresses where disclosed for location filtering, and flag certification status (current vs. expired). No affordable flat-file competitor exists below $1,000 on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell custom-built lists with per-contact pricing at $0.10-$2.00 which scales to $13,000-$260,000 for full 130K USREPS registry, or require enterprise contact for volume pricing, creating massive wedge opportunity for one-time $149 CSV that undercuts vendor pricing by 87×-1,745×. Score is 7 due to strong validated commercial vendor ecosystem (6+ vendors with documented $0.10-$2.00/contact pricing), excellent public data availability via USREPS as purpose-built public registry for 130K+ certified professionals, multiple high-LTV B2B buyer segments (gym software at $1,428-$4,788/year LTV, fitness equipment at $5,000-$50,000 packages, CE courses at $200-$800/year recurring spend per trainer), massive TAM (130K+ certified professionals in USREPS, 384K+ total fitness professionals per BLS), and 87×-1,745× cost advantage vs. vendor per-contact pricing. Score not higher than 7 due to: (a) fitness certifications are voluntary credentials (not state-mandated professional licenses like LCSW or RN), meaning USREPS registry may under-represent total fitness professional population (many trainers work uncertified or with non-NCCA-accredited certifications not included in USREPS), (b) buyer LTV slightly lower than healthcare software verticals (gym software at $1,428-$4,788/year vs. EHR software at $3,600-$7,200+/year), and (c) fitness industry has higher churn (trainers moving between employment settings, leaving industry, or letting certifications lapse) compared to licensed professions with mandatory continuing education, though this is partially offset by large TAM and strong CE provider demand for databases to market recertification courses.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all currently certified fitness professionals extracted from the United States Registry of Exercise Professionals (USREPS) maintained by CREP, plus supplemental data from NASM credential verification directory and ACSM professional finder — fully public certification registries with zero authentication barriers. Each record includes the professional's full name, primary certification credential (Certified Personal Trainer CPT, Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist CSCS, Certified Exercise Physiologist, Certified Group Fitness Instructor GFI, Health Coach, Clinical Exercise Physiologist), certifying organization (ACE, NASM, ACSM, NSCA, AFAA, ISSA, and 20+ NCCA-accredited member orgs), additional credentials and specializations (Corrective Exercise Specialist CES, Performance Enhancement Specialist PES, Nutrition Coach, Senior Fitness Specialist, Youth Fitness Specialist, Pre/Postnatal Specialist), certification status (current vs. expired), initial certification date, geographic location (city/state where disclosed), and professional setting (independent trainer, gym employee, studio owner, online coach where available). As of 2026, USREPS registry contains 130,000+ currently certified exercise and medical fitness professionals with NCCA-accredited or ISO 17024-compliant certifications from member organizations, with broader fitness industry employment at 384,000+ fitness trainers and instructors per BLS, and commercial vendor databases confirming 25,000-67,000 verified personal trainer contacts. Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) Gym management and fitness studio software vendors (Mindbody serving 70K+ fitness businesses at $119-$399/month generating $1,428-$4,788/year LTV, Zen Planner, Glofox, TrueCoach, Wodify for CrossFit boxes, Pike13, ClubReady) pay $3,000-$8,000/year for certified personal trainer databases to acquire gym/studio owners and independent trainers as software customers; (2) Fitness equipment manufacturers (Rogue Fitness, TRX, Peloton, Precor, Life Fitness, Concept2, Assault Fitness, Keiser) selling to personal trainers building home studios and small training facilities with equipment packages at $5,000-$50,000; (3) Fitness continuing education providers (NASM with 50+ CE courses at $99-$699 each, ACE, ISSA, Precision Nutrition at $999-$1,299, NSCA, AFAA specializations) selling mandatory recertification credits — NASM requires 2.0 CEUs or 20 hours every 2 years, ACE requires 2.0 CEUs over 2 years, creating recurring $200-$800/year CE spend per certified trainer to maintain credentials and add specializations; (4) Fitness business services (K&K Insurance professional liability at $150-$400/year, online coaching platforms like Trainerize at $5-$60/month, nutrition software, client assessment tools, marketing agencies, merchant services). A one-time $149 CSV undercuts traditional B2B data vendors (InfoGlobalData documenting $0.10-$2.00 per contact which scales to $13,000-$260,000 for full 130K registry, other vendors requiring enterprise contact for volume pricing) by 87×-1,745× while targeting identical buyer segments.

data_wanted: United States Registry of Exercise Professionals (USREPS) at usreps.org/registry/ maintained by CREP (Commission on Reforming Exercise Professionals) is the primary public registry listing 130,000+ currently certified exercise and medical fitness professionals — anyone earning an NCCA accredited or ISO 17024-compliant certification from member organizations is automatically registered in USREPS free of charge. Registry is fully public and searchable with zero authentication required, designed explicitly for healthcare providers, employers, gyms, and the public to find and verify certified professionals. USREPS member organizations include: American Council on Exercise (ACE) with 90,000+ certified professionals, National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) with 1.9M+ certified pros, American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM), National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA), Athletics and Fitness Association of America (AFAA), International Sports Sciences Association (ISSA), International Fitness Professionals Association (IFPA), National Council for Certified Personal Trainers (NCCPT), National Exercise and Sports Trainers Association (NESTA), American Fitness Professionals & Associates (AFPA), International Youth Conditioning Association (IYCA), USA Weightlifting (USAW), and 15+ additional NCCA-accredited certifying bodies. Supplemental public directories: NASM maintains credential verification directory at directory.nasm.org and verification tool at nasm.org/resources/validate-credentials enabling employers and gyms to verify NASM certified personal trainers; ACSM provides Find an ACSM Certified Professional directory at acsm.org/certification/professional-resources/profinder/ for locating ACSM certified exercise professionals and clinical exercise physiologists. Key fields per professional: Full name (first, middle initial, last), primary credential or certification (Certified Personal Trainer CPT, Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist CSCS, Certified Clinical Exercise Physiologist, Certified Group Fitness Instructor GFI, Certified Health Coach, Exercise Physiologist EP-C, Tactical Strength and Conditioning Facilitator TSAC-F), certifying organization (ACE, NASM, ACSM, NSCA, AFAA, ISSA, NCCPT, NESTA, IFPA), additional credentials and specializations (Corrective Exercise Specialist CES, Performance Enhancement Specialist PES, Certified Nutrition Coach CNC, Senior Fitness Specialist, Youth Fitness Specialist, Pre/Postnatal Exercise Specialist, Sports Performance Coach, Certified Functional Strength Coach CFSC, CrossFit Level 1 or Level 2 where disclosed, TRX qualified trainer, USA Weightlifting coach, FMS certified), certification status (currently certified vs. expired or lapsed), initial certification date (year of first credential), recertification date or expiration date (most certifications require renewal every 2-3 years with continuing education), geographic location (city, state, zip code where disclosed — availability varies by certifying organization and individual privacy settings), professional setting or employment type (independent personal trainer, gym employee, studio owner, online coach, corporate wellness, military or government, clinical or hospital-based where disclosed), and credential verification number or ID (where provided by certifying organization for employer verification). Target all currently certified professionals with active credentials (exclude expired certifications unless specifically requested for recertification marketing by CE providers). Approximately 130,000+ currently certified professionals in USREPS registry (conservative count of NCCA-accredited credentials only), with broader fitness industry employment estimated at 384,000+ fitness trainers and instructors per BLS May 2023 Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (includes non-certified instructors, group fitness instructors working without certification, yoga/Pilates instructors with non-NCCA credentials, and uncertified trainers). Commercial vendor databases (BookYourData 25,419 contacts, Scrap.io claiming 67K fitness professionals) suggest addressable market between USREPS minimum of 130K and BLS maximum of 384K. Target output: 150K rows, one row per professional (individuals with multiple certifications from different organizations like ACE-CPT plus NASM-CES may appear as separate entries per credential or consolidated by name). Data is 100% public — fitness certifications are voluntary professional credentials maintained by private certification organizations, with USREPS explicitly designed as public registry to enable employers, healthcare providers, and consumers to find and verify certified exercise professionals. No privacy restrictions under professional credentialing transparency standards.
